title: FogBank sovereign connectivity and onprem edge intake
summary: Initial intake with FogBank to understand sovereign requirements, multi‑region constraints, and an on‑prem edge gateway option. Main concerns: data residency, BYO KMS, egress IPs, transit gateway alternatives across Azure+AWS, and an air‑gapped fallback plan.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-02
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Samir Nair (CTO, FogBank), Lena Ortiz (Infra), Marta Ruiz (Security), Daniel Ko (Network)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. Quick intros?
[00:06] Samir: Hi I'm Samir, CTO at FogBank, we run a regulated data analytics platform for public sector and enterprise finance. We're looking at Redwood for inference — main thing is sovereign requirements and also an option to run an edge gateway on prem for low-latency inference.
[00:18] Priya: Thanks Samir. Quick note — we'll try to map architecture patterns to your constraints today and surface tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated and Private modes, but it sounds like you're leaning Private.
[00:28] Lena: Yep, leaning Private. Our security folks want residency in three countries — US, UK, and Germany — and some workloads must not leave their regional VPC.
[00:36] Marta: And we need BYO KMS for key handling and HSM-backed signing for tokens. Also heavy audit logs.
[00:44] Alex: Totally reasonable. Before we dive, can you walk us through current infra — clouds, transit, and how you think traffic would flow to Redwood?
[00:52] Daniel: Sure. We are multi-cloud — dev on GCP, prod clusters split between AWS (main) and Azure (EU). We use a transit gateway in AWS, cloud WAN in Azure, and we have SD-WAN backhaul to our two on‑prem edge PoPs.
[01:05] Priya: Ok, when you say on‑prem edge PoPs — are you expecting Redwood to host an appliance/VM in those PoPs or do you want a private endpoint to your VPCs?
[01:13] Samir: Ideally both. For latency-critical customers we want an on‑prem inference gateway in the PoP that can call Redwood Dedicated in-region as a control plane, but the dataplane for model execution stays in an approved region or on-prem if needed.
[01:27] Alex: So a hybrid dataplane option. That's doable — Redwood Private supports a customer-managed dataplane + control plane split. We usually recommend private endpoints peered to our control plane and optionally a relay/gateway inside customer network for low-latency.
[01:40] Marta: How do we prove keys never leave our KMS? We have a FIPS HSM.
[01:45] Priya: We support BYO KMS integrations — you can provision keys via KMIP or cloud KMS with HSM-backed keys. For fully air‑gapped HSM we can sign tokens on premise and only send signed assertions to the control plane; we have patterns in the runbook. We'll send a short runbook after this call.
[01:59] Daniel: Network constraints — we need predictable egress IPs for allowlisting. We also have scenarios where we can't do cross-border peering; that means we need separate deployments per region with strict routing.
[02:09] Alex: Understood. Redwood can provide static egress IP ranges for Private deployments (per-region). There's an option for IP slicing — if you need multiple egress blocks per customer or per environment.
[02:20] Samir: Are those egress IPs fixed for the lifetime of a deploy? We have compliance requiring stable allowlists for months.
[02:26] Priya: For Dedicated and Private, yes — we can reserve static egress IPs for the deployment window and document them. For Hosted we can't guarantee long-term fixed IPs.
[02:36] Lena: What about cross-cloud peering? Our prod interacts across AWS and Azure; we'd prefer not to open the whole transit gateway to external peers.
[02:44] Priya: Options: 1) VPC/VNet peering per region into a dedicated Redwood Private VPC (works well if you own the routing), 2) use an ingress/egress proxy inside your transit — we can support an appliance model (VM or containerized gateway) that connects to Redwood control plane via private link, 3) use carrier/VPN stitching for air-gapped PoPs. Each has tradeoffs.
[03:05] Daniel: What's the latency hit for proxy/gateway? If the gateway is in the same PoP as the client it's small, but if control plane is remote...
[03:12] Priya: If you localize the model execution to that region or on prem, we can keep token latency under 20–50ms for short requests; typical generative calls vary. But there is an overhead if you backhaul to another region. We'll share a latency matrix.
[03:24] Samir: Ok. Two more things — audit retention and network logging for forensics. We need at least 1 year of immutable logs.
[03:33] Alex: We provide audit logs and write them to your S3/GCS buckets or to our secure retention; for Private we can push to your bucket in-region. Immutability depends on your bucket policies. We can support append-only retention and sign logs.
[03:44] Marta: Good. Also need SSO + SCIM provisioning and RBAC integration with our identity provider.
[03:50] Priya: Redwood integrates with SAML/SSO and SCIM for user provisioning, plus fine-grained RBAC. We'll share the integration guide.
[03:58] Alex: Let's talk timeline and pilot definition — what would success look like for this project?
[04:03] Samir: Success = proof that we can host inference for a sensitive classifier inside EU and UK with BYO KMS, egress allowlist, and under 100ms p95 latency for up to 10qps per customer. If that passes, we plan to onboard three customers in Q3.
[04:17] Priya: That sounds actionable. Pilot steps: 1) network intake and allowlist. 2) deploy a non-prod Private instance in EU region with a single small GPU model. 3) run perf tests and validate KMS flow and logs. 4) security review.
[04:30] Daniel: For the network intake, what info do you need from us?
[04:33] Alex: We'll need VPC/VNet CIDRs, peering preferences, preferred AZs, firewall egress rules, and a contact for the networking team. Also whether you want transit‑gateway peering or a dedicated peer.
[04:45] Daniel: We'll pull the current network diagram and a list of public IP ranges we can use for allowlisting.
[04:49] Marta: On the compliance side, send us SOC2 and ISO artifact list and your penetration testing cadence.
[04:54] Alex: We'll attach the SOC2 and ISO summaries and also our penetration testing schedule.
[04:58] Samir: Two technical clarifications — 1) can Redwood run a lightweight inference runtime on our PoPs that does quantized models without sending KV cache to Redwood control plane? 2) if we need air-gap for some customers can we keep model weights on prem and only call control plane for billing/monitoring?
[05:12] Priya: 1) yes, we have an edge runtime for inference that supports quantized model execution — there are tradeoffs with model size and latency but it's supported. 2) We can support a fully air-gapped dataplane where weights and execution stay on prem; the control plane can be replaced with an ephemeral control path or offline billing. Those are more advanced deployments and require an engineering engagement, but doable.
[05:29] Samir: What about updates and rollouts for models if weights live on prem?
[05:33] Priya: We recommend a signed bundle distribution. Your security team signs acceptance and the edge runtime verifies bundles before applying. We have a signed-bundle pattern in our private deployment playbook.
[05:43] Daniel: Regarding IP slices — do you charge per egress block? We have many environments and would prefer consolidated billing.
[05:49] Alex: Egress IP blocks are a configuration item; pricing is tied to capacity and support, not per-IP. We'll outline options in the proposal.
[05:58] Marta: Data residency — if we deploy separate instances per country, how do you handle global model updates and model drift monitoring?
[06:05] Priya: For region‑isolated deployments we can roll model versions independently per instance. We also support a metrics aggregation pipeline that can forward anonymized metrics to a central Redwood instance if you permit — otherwise we provide per-region dashboards.
[06:18] Samir: Anything else we should be aware of from your side?
[06:21] Alex: From a block list — we'll need an approved maintenance window for kernel updates on edge runtimes; security patches will require coordination. Also, for pilot we'll ask for a small service account with minimal privileges to validate the KMS integration.
[06:34] Lena: Who owns the transit costs for cross-cloud peering?
[06:37] Alex: Typically customer covers cloud egress/peering costs; Redwood covers managed private endpoint infrastructure costs. We'll itemize in the proposal.
[06:45] Daniel: Any restrictions on ports and protocols for the edge gateway?
[06:48] Priya: Minimal: outbound TLS to control plane on 443, optional mTLS on custom port for control messages, and a few ports for health and metrics. We'll send exact port list.
[06:59] Samir: Ok that helps. Quick objection — in our RFP we have a question around vendor lock-in: if we go with Redwood Private how portable are our configs and models?
[07:08] Priya: We try to avoid lock-in — we support standard model formats (ONNX, torchscript), and configs are YAML/JSON that you can export. For fully managed features that are Redwood-specific we'll document export paths. For air-gapped, since weights stay on prem, portability is high.
[07:24] Alex: Anything from a legal/procurement angle we should know?
[07:28] Marta: We'll need a data processing addendum, standard SLAs, and an audit clause.
[07:33] Alex: We'll include a draft DPA and SLA in the materials.
[07:36] Samir: Ok, next steps?
[07:38] Alex: Action items: we'll send architecture + SOC2/ISO docs by Monday (3/6). Priya will prep BYO KMS runbook and port list by Friday (3/5). FogBank will share network diagram and list of required regions by 3/9. Then we schedule a technical deep dive week of 3/12.
[07:54] Marta: Sounds good. Also we'll assign a legal contact and send procurement windows.
[07:59] Alex: Great, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep dive. Thanks everyone.
[08:03] Samir: Thanks Alex and Priya, appreciate it.

Notes on transcript: occasional dropped words and name substitutions in auto-transcript, e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' transcribed as 'Redwood dedicate' at times. There were short crosstalk moments around 03:00–03:30 when network team chimed in.

End of transcript.
